title: Two local perfect models at a common stage
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, R:I → CommRingCat a system of Noetherian rings, c a cocone, i an index, and s:Xi → Spec R_i locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Choose shared derived module categories on schemes and their open localizations [def-pc-derived-category]. Let W,V be opens of Xi, W compact and V affine, with PerfectDescentOnOpen R c i Xi s W and PerfectDescentOnOpen R c i Xi s V [def-pc-perfect-descent-on-open]. Let f:Z → Xi be an open immersion with image W union V, t=f followed by s, and E a perfect complex on X=Z times_{R_i} c.pt [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Then some j≥i admits a two-open cover U,V of Y=Z times_{R_i} R_j with U and V compact, perfect objects A on U and B on V, and isomorphisms L(g_j|U)^*A ≅ E|_{g_j inverse U} and L(g_j|V)^*B ≅ E|_{g_j inverse V}, using canonical derived open restriction [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps] and the canonical base-change map g_j induced by c_j. No colimit proof, overlap isomorphism, or direct-image adjoint map is asserted.

proof.text: Apply the one-open eventual model theorem to W and V, using the two inclusions into the image supplied by f.opensRange = W sup V. Choose an upper bound k of the two resulting stages by directedness. Evaluate both eventual model families at k. Proof irrelevance identifies the two proofs i <= k, so both model comparisons use the same canonical base-change map.

Use U = (stage projection followed by f) inverse W and Vprime = (stage projection followed by f) inverse V. Their join is top because the inverse image of f.opensRange along f is top and inverse image preserves joins. The compact image of f is the compact union W union V, making Z compact. Xi is quasi-separated since s is quasi-separated over an affine scheme; therefore f is quasi-compact. The stage projection is quasi-compact as a base change of an affine morphism between affine schemes. The composite is quasi-compact, so inverse images of compact W and V are compact. Package these geometric facts with the two perfect objects and their comparisons.

theorem perfect_descent_common_local_models
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [∀ i : I, IsNoetherianRing (R.obj i)]
    (c : Cocone R) (i : I) (Xi : Scheme.{u}) (s : Xi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation s] [QuasiCompact s] [QuasiSeparated s]
    [∀ Z : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (U : Z.Opens),
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (W V : Xi.Opens) (hW : IsCompact (W : Set Xi)) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (dW : PerfectDescentOnOpen R c i Xi s W)
    (dV : PerfectDescentOnOpen R c i Xi s V)
    (Z : Scheme.{u}) (f : Z ⟶ Xi) [IsOpenImmersion f] (hf : f.opensRange = W ⊔ V)
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory (pullback (f ≫ s) (Spec.map (c.ι.app i))))
    (hE : (pullback (f ≫ s) (Spec.map (c.ι.app i))).IsPerfect E) :
    ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j),
      let Y := pullback (f ≫ s) (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij)))
      let X := pullback (f ≫ s) (Spec.map (c.ι.app i))
      let g := baseChangeMap (f ≫ s)
        (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
        (T' := Over.mk (Spec.map (c.ι.app i)))
        (Over.homMk (Spec.map (c.ι.app j))
          (by dsimp; rw [← Spec.map_comp, c.w (homOfLE hij)]))
      ∃ (U V : Y.Opens), U ⊔ V = ⊤ ∧
        IsCompact (U : Set Y) ∧ IsCompact (V : Set Y) ∧
      ∃ (A : schemeDerivedCategory U.toScheme) (B : schemeDerivedCategory V.toScheme),
        U.toScheme.IsPerfect A ∧ V.toScheme.IsPerfect B ∧
        Nonempty ((derivedPullback (g ∣_ U)).obj A ≅
          (schemeOpenRestriction X (g ⁻¹ᵁ U)).mapDerivedCategory.obj E) ∧
        Nonempty ((derivedPullback (g ∣_ V)).obj B ≅
          (schemeOpenRestriction X (g ⁻¹ᵁ V)).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)
